chunks.arabic_text: عَلِيُّ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ، الْهَرْمُزَانِيُّ، أَبُو الْحَسَنِ. قُمِيّ. ضَعِيفٌ.

translations.en: Ali ibn Ja'far, al-Hurmuzani, Abu al-Hasan. Qummi. Weak.

en.summary: This entry from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Ghada'iri’s *Kitab al- Duafa* identifies Ali ibn Ja'far al-Hurmuzani, a narrator from Qum, as weak (da'if) in hadith transmission. His designation as 'Qummi' highlights the importance of regional scholarly networks in early Shia hadith criticism, while his relative obscurity underscores the rigorous scrutiny applied even to those connected to prominent families like the Banu Ja'far.
en.seo_question: Who is Ali ibn Ja'far al-Hurmuzani and what is his status as a hadith narrator?

key_terms.قُمِيّ: A person originating from the city of Qum
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak (referring to the reliability of a narrator in hadith sciences)
key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan (a kunya or honorific name meaning 'Father of al-Hasan')
